mechaber/1:main: Fruit juice is fine if sour. And there are 7 sections: fruit water without water is not sour at all and it is permissible to eat matza on Passover that has been soaked in fruit water even if it has been tea all day, but one does not go out of his way to eat it because it is a rich matza and read the caption for poverty bread:
mechaber/2:main: Fruit juice with water accelerates chametzing more than other dough; therefore one should not knead with them, and if one kneaded with them one should bake immediately.
mechaber/3:main: It is permitted to knead with wine even though it is impossible without a drop of water that falls at the time of pressing; even l'chatchila it is customary to put water at the time of pressing in order to permit via connecting flow; nevertheless we are not concerned about them, since the water was already nullified in the wine before they kneaded the dough.
mechaber/4:main: Egg liquid and all other liquids are included in fruit juice. {Rama: And in these countries it is not customary to knead with fruit juice, and even to shape the matzot it is not customary except after they are baked while still hot; one should not deviate from this unless in a time of need — for the needs of a sick person or an elderly person who requires this.}
mechaber/5:main: When kneading dough in fruit juice, it is good to make it less than the measure of an isaron so that one not become obligated in challah.
mechaber/6:main: Wheat found in honey, or in wine and vinegar, is permitted, provided water has not mixed into them.
mechaber/7:main: The salt must be checked before Passover to make sure there are no needles in it, because when the salt gets wet, it gets into the needles little by little and turns sour:
